readme: Ten dictations a reader might plausibly make, written so that between them they exercise every source a vocabulary can be built from. `hard` lists the terms whose spelling is the point — recall is scored on those, and WER on the whole line. `slug` is the article in scope, which decides which glossary and which extracted names the article-level conditions get. The last one is the control: it says nothing hard at all, so any vocabulary term appearing in its transcript was invented.

utterances.text: The Müller-Lyer illusion does not show what he thinks it shows here. Predictive processing is doing all the work, and pareidolia is a separate claim about computational functionalism.
Worth checking whether Hinton would accept this. The Ex Machina reading of Ava feels like a distraction from the Turing point that Anil Seth is actually making.
Ranking philoprogenitiveness above combativeness tells you more about Victorian morals than about acquisitiveness, and veneration is barely argued for at all.
Alimentiveness barely gets a mention, but phrenology as a whole rests on it. Spurzheim was more careful than Gall, and Elliotson was not careful at all.

Corrigibility and the disposition dial are in tension. Anthropic wants Claude to be a transparent conscientious objector and also broadly safe, and sandbagging is the failure mode nobody has priced in.
Add this to Spideryarn please. The granularity zoom is fine but the gist column should follow the block id, which here is spya-k3m9qt.
My background is in cognitive science, and I have spent most of my working life on startups, so the software engineering parts are the easy bit for me.

utterances.note: Most dictation is short. The plan's own eval README says the 22-second sample tells us nothing about short utterances, and a four-word one is where a transcriber has least context to work with.

utterances.why: Every hard term here comes from one place and one only: the reader's "why you're reading this one" box. None of them is in the article, in its glossary, in the profile or in the site terms — checked by grep against every blocks.json and glossary.json in data/. So this clip scores zero on every condition that does not read that box, which is what makes it a measurement of the box rather than of the four sources around it.
utterances.text: Does this actually answer Vervaeke on relevance realisation? Worth sending to Anjali Chaudhuri before Thursday, and it bears on Friston too.
I think the second half of this is much weaker than the first. He keeps asserting things that need an argument, and by the end I had stopped believing the setup.
utterances.note: The harm probe, and the reason the whole eval exists rather than just a bigger vocabulary. Ordinary English, no jargon, dictated against an article whose vocabulary is loaded. Every vocabulary term that turns up in this transcript was invented by a model that had been told to expect it. If a large list makes this one worse, the list is too large — and no measurement of the other eight would have said so.
